correctness.rationale: With rows recording the coefficients of the natural basis squares, the matrix is block upper triangular with first block determinant (9-1)/16=1/2 and all other diagonal entries 1. This proves perfection over any field with 2 invertible, even when 3/4 vanishes. For the first two coordinates let S=x_1+x_2 and D=x_1-x_2. The equations give D(1-S/2)=0 and 2S=S^2+D^2. If D were nonzero one would have S=2 and then D^2=0, impossible in a field. Thus D=0 and x_1=x_2 is 0 or 1. For j>=3 the actual entries give x_j^2-x_j+h_j=0, h_3=x_1^2/4 and h_(j+1)=(3h_j+x_j^2)/4. If h_j=1/4 the unique root is 1/2 and preserves h; if h_j=0 the root 0 preserves it and the root 1 switches it to 1/4. There is one branch with initial pair (1,1); the other has either no switch or one first switch at k=3,...,n. This proves each listed coordinate vector, distinctness and exhaustion, including the empty tail at n=2. The derivation works unchanged over any extension, so the geometric points are all rational already over the prime field. Repeated roots are counted as one point, not by scheme length. The recorded rational and finite-field tests are supplementary; no uploaded code was executed.

value.rationale: This realizes the first count below the discussed triangular-construction threshold in every complex dimension n>=3 and gives explicitly the full rational point list in all odd characteristics as well. The dimension-two seed followed by forced repeated-root extensions is a reusable construction mechanism. It resolves an infinite set of motivated spectrum instances without claiming a lower bound for other algebras or the remaining cardinalities of the conjecture.
